title: Issue summary: A QUIC server that rejects a stream opened by the peer may retain that stream's state for the lifetime…
description: A vulnerability in QUIC servers prior to version 3.1.7 allows a remote client to cause unbounded memory growth by repeatedly opening and resetting streams. This occurs because the server retains the state of rejected streams if the peer resets the stream before the rejection is signaled, leading to a denial of service due to memory exhaustion. The issue does not cause memory corruption or data disclosure and requires a long-lived connection for exploitation.
